about: Brixton market in the morning, then a walk round Crystal Palace Park and up through Anerley.

cards.line: Did you know, Brixton's Electric Avenue was the first market street lit by electricity?
cards.fact: Electric Avenue in Brixton was the first market street to be lit by electricity. Eddy Grant's 1982 hit song Electric Avenue is named after it.

cards.line: Did you know, the marble gorilla by Crystal Palace's lake is a portrait of London Zoo's Guy?
cards.fact: The black marble gorilla by the lake is Guy, a London Zoo favourite. He reached the zoo on Guy Fawkes Day 1947, which is how he got his name.

cards.line: Did you know, a dinner party was once held inside a dinosaur in Crystal Palace Park?
cards.fact: To launch the world's first dinosaur sculptures, their maker held a dinner on New Year's Eve 1853 inside the mould of one of the Iguanodons. The sculptures are still in the park.

cards.place: Crystal Palace Bowl, Crystal Palace Park
cards.line: Did you know, the Who's drummer once served tea and cake from a rowing boat in Crystal Palace Park?
cards.fact: Hosting a 1972 concert at the park's stage, the Who's drummer Keith Moon flew in by helicopter, then rowed the lake dressed as a pirate, serving tea.

cards.line: Did you know, an Indian MP who lived in Anerley swore his oath to Parliament on a Zoroastrian holy book?
cards.fact: Dadabhai Naoroji lived on Anerley Park from 1897. Elected an MP in 1892 by just 5 votes, he swore his oath on a Zoroastrian holy book, not the Bible.

about: South by car: errands in Croydon, past West Wickham, a walk on Keston Common, then Downe.

cards.line: Did you know, the distress call Mayday was invented at Croydon Airport?
cards.fact: In the early 1920s, Croydon Airport's head of radio needed a distress call that pilots and Paris controllers would both understand. He chose Mayday, because it sounds like the French for help me.

cards.line: Did you know, West Wickham's old manor house was built for a man who married an Anne Boleyn?
cards.fact: Wickham Court was built in 1469 for Sir Henry Heydon, whose wife was Anne Boleyn. Not the queen, but her great-aunt of the same name.

cards.line: Did you know, Charles Darwin studied plants and animals on Keston Common for his books?
cards.fact: Darwin's home at Down House was 2 miles away, and he often came to study the common's wildlife for his books on earthworms and meat-eating plants.

cards.line: Did you know, Darwin's family turned their backs during one creed at Downe church?
cards.fact: Charles Darwin's wife Emma was a Unitarian. So whenever the church's Trinity creed was read at St Mary's, the family turned to face away.

cards.line: Did you know, Darwin wrote On the Origin of Species in a village that's now part of London?
cards.fact: Charles Darwin wrote On the Origin of Species in his study at Down House, in Downe. It was Kent then; since 1965 it has been in the London Borough of Bromley.

about: A day off going east: Chislehurst, Petts Wood, the train from Elmstead Woods, then Sidcup and Bexleyheath.

cards.line: Did you know, David Bowie and Jimi Hendrix played gigs deep inside Chislehurst Caves?
cards.fact: The man-made caves under Chislehurst, old chalk mines, were a rock venue in the 1960s. David Bowie played there four times between 1962 and 1966, and Jimi Hendrix twice.

cards.line: Did you know, the story goes that summer time was dreamed up on a ride in Petts Wood?
cards.fact: The story goes that builder William Willett got the idea seeing blinds still down one summer morning. His memorial is a sundial set to summer time.

cards.line: Did you know, 50 million year old sharks' teeth lie in a pit opposite Elmstead Woods station?
cards.fact: The pit across from the station shows a layer laid down in an estuary 50 million years ago. It holds fossil sharks' teeth, shells and fish scales.

cards.line: Did you know, Frognal House became a major First World War centre for rebuilding soldiers' faces?
cards.fact: In 1917 the mansion became the first home of Queen's Hospital, the war's major centre for facial and plastic surgery. It admitted 5,000 men by 1921.

cards.line: Did you know, William Morris drew his first wallpapers at a house in Bexleyheath with no wallpaper?
cards.fact: The designer William Morris drew his earliest wallpapers at Red House, the only house he ever built. Yet there was to be no wallpaper in it: the walls were painted or hung with tapestries.

about: Penge High Street errands, Hayes, Keston church, then Eltham and Blackheath in the evening.

cards.line: Did you know, Penge's name comes from the language that later became Welsh?
cards.fact: Penge's name is Brittonic, the language that became Welsh, and means head of the wood. A charter of 957 mentions the wood called Penge.

cards.line: Did you know, an enslaved Native American man is buried in Hayes churchyard?
cards.fact: John Panis was brought to England as a slave and died in 1763. Panis was the general word for an enslaved Native American.
cards.source: Wikipedia: St Mary the Virgin, Hayes, Bromley

cards.line: Did you know, Keston's medieval church has no saint, just a cross called the Keston Marke?
cards.fact: Keston's medieval church, unusually, isn't named after a saint. Its symbol instead is an ornate cross inlaid in its 17th-century altar top.

cards.line: Did you know, Eltham Palace's great hall, where Parliaments met, became a barn?
cards.fact: Edward IV finished the great hall at Eltham Palace around 1479, and Parliaments met there. By the 1790s, the royal hall was being used as a barn.
cards.source: BHO: RCHME London vol 5; Lysons, Environs of London vol 4

cards.line: Did you know, an emperor from Constantinople was welcomed to England on Blackheath?
cards.fact: On 21 December 1400, Henry IV met the emperor of Constantinople, now Istanbul, on Blackheath. He'd come to ask for help against the Turks, the only emperor from there ever to visit England.
